Final full-distribution pairs run Node streaming before/after, Bun buffered after/before, then Bun streaming before/after. Percentile ranges span the two driver values, not pooled requests.
ssrSchedulingComparison.bunReproduction: Build the committed Bun adapter. Clone its dist into two local trees. In the control only, transpile render-scheduler.ts from the control commit using workspace TypeScript ES2022/ESNext into render-scheduler.js. Select the before/after adapter through the benchmark worker import. Preserve all other host, renderer and load-driver code. Source maps are not used for measurement. Verify participant and adapter hashes before and after every case. Final full-distribution controls retain the pre-extraction render-policy.js from c8711bfa, while changed adapters use 8a766808 including the shared work window. All final comparisons share the server build from 8a766808.

Give its checkpoint a streaming capability using Bun createBunRenderPolicy(gate, enqueue).streaming only while the Node gate shouldSchedule() is true. Initial admission and buffered rendering retain their existing behavior. That prototype precedes the committed shared work-window implementation. Final Node comparisons substitute only admission.js from c8711bfa for the before case, retaining the shared server build in both variants.

Restoring batching while retaining window bookkeeping recovers most of the loss. Both gate policies predominantly select scheduling, so the regression is in the selected checkpoint policy rather than failure to enable admission.

Baseline/current/current/baseline order, then current/fixed/fixed/current for the repair. Ranges span per-driver P99 values, not pooled request percentiles.
ssrDocumentComparison.baselineBuild: Substitute the three listed files from the baseline revision. Transpile document-output.ts into its package output with workspace TypeScript. ssrDocumentComparison.cpuMethod: Process CPU delta divided by completed-response delta, from the telemetry sample nearest the end of warmup to the final sample.

methodology.memory: Cumulative allocated bytes and allocation count per compilation, not retained heap or peak RSS.

methodology.timingBudget: Unchanged historical cold baseline 1816.057 ms, incremental baseline 371.256 ms and warning maximum 1.5. The guard is the larger of the cold and incremental project ratios. This optimization targets a guard below 1.0 without rebasing either measurement.

cold.method: Same local Go test harness for both committed production variants. One full cold-project compile, with Go CPU and allocation profiles. No per-file logging. Test-harness setup and GC are included.
cold.limit: Approximate cumulative sampled allocations, not peak or retained heap. Cumulative stack rows overlap and must not be added.

geography.method: Warm one synchronized session by compiling all 34 modules. Start CPU profiling only after warmup. Append a further newline to the same prepared geography request for each of ten edits. Read runtime total allocations around each edit and subtract warmup allocation profiles from the final allocation profile.
geography.observedWork: Each edit still invalidates 34 sources, analyzes 17 callable sources and rebuilds the program once. The optimized ordinary-module request performs no component source analyses or placement link walks. Component requests compute the deferred fixed point from fresh facts.
geography.limit: This diagnostic repeats edits in one retained session and includes profiling overhead. It is separate from the accepted fresh-session incremental populations.
geography.allocationFinding: Registry identity checks still materialize the imported centroid array type. The coreImportExpression stack accounts for about 434 MiB, roughly 56% of the sampled allocation delta across ten optimized edits. This cumulative stack overlaps other rows.

completeEditPass.method: Each of three fresh JSON-protocol sessions per compiler synchronizes and compiles all 34 prepared sources outside the timer. The timer includes one geography newline edit followed by requesting all 34 modules again in corpus order, using the edited geography overlay. It includes protocol transport and response parsing, and excludes process startup and warmup. Baseline runs precede optimized runs without order reversal.
completeEditPass.limit: Local diagnostic, not a historical guard or counterbalanced population. The complete pass includes the component requests that perform deferred placement work.

limitations: One owned application on one host, two reversed populations and three samples per accepted measurement. No confidence interval or whole-corpus speed claim.
Syntax-mode corpus timings exclude semantic generated-code validation, SDK transport, bundlers and runtime execution. Semantic compiler correctness is verified separately.
Whitespace changes in one prepared source do not represent every authored or dependency edit. Component placement work is deferred to the next component request, not removed from that request.

Production implementations were committed and the root worktree was clean during accepted populations. Profiling uses ignored local Go test harnesses in isolated source copies, so diagnostic profiles are not clean-checkout benchmark runs. The baseline and optimized native source copies match their recorded overlay revisions and identical upstream Go source files.
Raw profiles, captures, local profiling harnesses and complete responses remain ignored local artifacts.
